I'm reconsidering 14...e4 as the more forcing option—after 15. dxe4, I could try 15...Rd2 to invade, though White has defensive resources like 16. Qf5+ and 17. Re2. Between the two candidate moves, e4 feels more dynamic and gives me better practical chances than the solid 14...Rd5. play. After dxe4, my rooks can become more active.

Hmm, but actually, after 14...e4 15. Qxe4, the queen takes the pawn. Then I'm down even more material. Unless I have a tactic. After Qxe4... Rd1 threatening Rxe1. 16. Qb7 is checkmate? No, Qb7+ Kd8 and it's not mate. 

Let me check: 14...e4 15. Qxe4 Rd4 16. Qf5+ Kb8 (or g6). After 16...Kb8 17. Qxf7 and White is winning easily.

OK so 14...e4 15. Qxe4 is just bad. What about 15. dxe4 instead? Then Rd2 with counterplay.

But White would likely just capture with the queen to win the pawn cleanly. Let me look at 14...Rd5 instead—it's more forcing, putting immediate pressure on the knight. After 15. Ne4, the knight becomes dangerous but at least my rook is actively placed. If 15. Na6, I can take with bxa6, though that damages my pawn structure. I think Rd5 is the natural try here, but I'm still essentially down a queen for a pawn, so the position is practically lost.

content.text: White recaptured with 14. Qxf3. I'm in a tough material deficit, but I need to stay active. I'll play 14...Rd5, attacking the knight on c5 and centralizing my rook on an active square. This forces the knight to relocate and keeps my pieces coordinated.
